contact_edits.before: Michael Gianfrescos sets give us two lots of painted bookshelves, especially unhelpful in Prague where they're supposed to house Jan's LPs; these remain undisturbed even after the secret police have paid a supposedly devastating visit. The scenes of crackdown are altogether lacking in threat. That leaves the music which, even to a rock skeptic like me, is invigorating, as well as cunningly selected for thematic relevance (some wag has suggested a soundtrack album, which is a very good idea) though it does play down rock's more aggressive side. Its peace and lover, brother, even now. The play ends with the Rolling Stones playing a breakthrough concert in the Czech capital. Jan and Esme are present. Max isn't, though his opinions on the validity of a visiting millionaire pop group as a symbol of liberation might be very interesting. - Rock 'n' Roll is at the Bluma Appel Theatre in Toronto through Oct. 24. For more information, visit canstage.comor call 416-368-3110. The production moves to the Citadel Theatre in Edmonton on Nov. 4; visit citadeltheatre.comor call 780-425-1820. robert.cushman@hotmail.com
